messages:
Sam: FYI I pushed a perf snapshot from the failing 16-node pipeline run — we're seeing long tail all-reduces that align with KV cache eviction spikes. NVLink-local ranks hit 3x latency compared to prior baseline.
Rachel: Can you paste the profiler slices? small numbers matter here. :eyes:
Sam: Dump (relevant lines):
```
# timeline (ms)
rank 0: compute 0.9 | allreduce 1.2 | kv-evict 0.4 | wait 6.8
rank 1 (nvlink-local): compute 1.0 | allreduce 8.4 | wait 0.6
rank 2 (pci-e hop): compute 0.7 | allreduce 2.1 | kv-prefetch 0.1
```
Notice rank1 spikes during the same step that triggers a KV eviction on rank0. Allreduce time jumps when NVLink path contends with the eviction DMA.
Miguel: Interesting — that smells like DMA/PCIe oversubscription when the eviction moves memory off-GPU. Could be our async eviction poking the fabric. Are we running eviction on CPU pinned buffers?
Sam: Yes, eviction uses host staging via pinned allocation, triggered by kvcache pressure. We recently changed the prefetch heuristics to be more aggressive (prefetch ahead 3 -> 6 segments). Might be the change.
Priya: Two quick checks: 1) is NCCL using NVLS (nvlink) vs p2p? check `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE` and `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` settings. 2) what's the kernel selection for allreduce payload sizes ~ 400KB? Small allreduces often fall back to tree instead of ring and can blow up latency.
Sam: Ran a quick NCCL run: `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=0 NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL` — but still saw the spike. payload ~ 420KB.
Rachel: If allreduce is using a tree algorithm because of small-frag sizes combined with asynchronous DMA bursts, we can get bad head-of-line blocking. Could we coalesce KV eviction I/O to off-peak windows or throttle eviction rate?
Miguel: Another angle: pipeline-parallel scheduling packs microbatches tightly to maximize compute overlap. If eviction I/O interrupts the NVSwitch fabric at the exact moment of reduce, the overlap becomes negative. We should try shifting KV eviction to a dedicated background stream pinned to a non-NVL path (force PCIe) to avoid contending with NVLink.
Priya: Proposed experiment plan:
- reproduce with current prefetch=6 and collect nvlink counters (ethstats/nvlink counters)
- run variant A: prefetch=3 (old)
- run variant B: prefetch=6 + eviction throttling (limits to 1 eviction per 8ms)
- run variant C: pin eviction host buffer to PCIe path / use cudaMemcpyAsync with stream mapped to CPU PCIe engine (force non-NVLINK DMA)
Tag each job with profiler collection.
Sam: I also added a kernel-selection probe: we log kernel choice for allreduces at runtime. For payloads 256-512KB current heuristics pick `ncclTreeTopo` which in our topology is a 3-hop pattern causing serialization. If we bias to `ncclRing` for these sizes on mesh-ish NVSwitch configs, it's ~2.5x lower median time in microbenchmarks.
Rachel: Good find. We need a topology-aware kernel selector: consider map of (rank->switch) and prefer ring when hops>1 OR when concurrent DMA > threshold. That avoids the pathological tree on partially connected sets.
Miguel: Also want to instrument KV cache so eviction events emit a short-lived "fabric pressure" metric. Scheduler can delay non-critical evictions when pressure>threshold.
Priya: Agree. Ops proposal: add a simple backoff: when `fabric_pressure > 0.7`, batch eviction requests and mark them as low-priority (use a separate eviction stream).
Sam: I'll open an RFC with these three mitigation patches: (1) kernel selector heuristic change, (2) eviction throttling + background stream, (3) profiler/signal for fabric pressure.
infra-bot: New RFC created: RFC-2026-evict-fabric-throttle (link: https://r.dev/rfc/2026) :white_check_mark:
Rachel: Thanks. Can someone run variant C on the smaller queue tonight and post results? If we see tail drop, we land throttle first.
Miguel: I'm on it. Starting a run now, will report by EOD. :thumbsup:
Priya: If it fixes it, follow-up: expose a per-deployment config for eviction aggressiveness and a console metric for fabric pressure so users can tune for Dedicated vs Hosted tiers.
Sam: Perfect. Will add config flag and console dashboard ticket to the RFC.
Rachel: Nice. Saving the profiler snippet to the issue. :memo:
